confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on aggregator and cost-of-living snapshots. Cappuccino and beer agree reasonably across sources; cocktail and wine rest on fewer data points, and the wine figure was set from a bar-price range. The midrange three-course figure is a judgement call, since one source's two-person estimate (about $45) looks low for three courses, so I kept it well above that. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and Boston context. No live booking pages or current listings were inspected. FX: I could not confirm the latest RBA observation on the generation date. The value used is the one shown on the RBA exchange-rates overview page in search results (as at 20 March 2026), which is older than the latest available observation. A third-party aggregator showed a later figure, but it is not an RBA source, so I did not use it.
comparable_city_reasoning: Boston-specific food and drink sources were used where available, cross-checked against general US major-city price levels. Accommodation uses a model estimate for a high-demand, high-cost US city in July.
